section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that teshuvah and Yom Kippur are in the category of the eighth, above the order of Hishtalshelus, with various levels of this eighth.
section.t: And this will be understood based on what is explained in the maamar
of Teshuvah
(and Atonement)
that they are in the category of the eighth, which is above the order of Hishtalshelus.
For great is teshuvah, which brings healing to the world,
and healing was established in the eighth,
for this that healing was established in the eighth is similar to
circumcision, which was given on the eighth.
And this is that seven days before Yom Kippur they separate the Kohen Gadol from his house,
and all seven days they accustom him to the services,
for the seven days are the category of Hishtalshelus,
and Yom Kippur,
the eighth day
(after the seven days)
is above Hishtalshelus.
And this is also the matter of the eight sprinklings on Yom Kippur: one above and seven below,
that the one that is above the seven is the category of "One I have asked,"
"One is My dove."
And from this it is understood
that in the eighth, which is above Hishtalshelus, there are several levels.
The eighth of circumcision, and similarly
the Holy of Holies, whose entry into the Holy of Holies is through the merit of circumcision.
The eighth of teshuvah, which is higher than the eighth of circumcision,
(for circumcision is a mitzvah,
and teshuvah, which atones for matters that damaged Torah and mitzvos, is above Torah and mitzvos
(as will be explained in section 8)).
The eighth of Yom Kippur,
for the teshuvah of Yom Kippur is loftier than the teshuvah of the entire year
(even from the teshuvah of the Ten Days of Repentance),
therefore Yom Kippur is a time of teshuvah for all,
and on Yom Kippur itself—the eight sprinklings in the Holy of Holies, one above and seven below,
that the one is before the seven.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section distinguishes between the eighth after the seven, which relates to Hishtalshelus, and the "one before the seven," which is utterly transcendent, explaining why "no man shall be" specifically in the Holy of Holies.
section.t: And it can be said,
that the eighth after the seven is a revelation above Hishtalshelus that is drawn down after and through the matters of Hishtalshelus,
and from the fact that the drawing down of this revelation is through the matters of Hishtalshelus, it is proven that this revelation is related to Hishtalshelus,
and the "one before the seven" is a revelation above Hishtalshelus that is above any connection to Hishtalshelus,
[except that afterward the revelation is drawn down into Hishtalshelus,
the seven after the one,
as will be explained in section 7].
And based on this, the reason will be understood for this that "and no man shall be" etc. is specifically when he comes to atone in the Holy,
for regarding the revelation that was in the Holy of Holies in its own right
[which is similar to the eighth of circumcision,
the eighth after the seven],
above Hishtalshelus that is related to Hishtalshelus,
there is a place for existence.
And through the service of the Kohen Gadol on Yom Kippur in the Holy of Holies, the revelation of that which is above Hishtalshelus and beyond any connection to Hishtalshelus is drawn down,
and regarding this revelation, "no man shall be,"
even those whose likeness of their faces is the face of man.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section introduces the concept that mitzvos draw down the revelation of the name Havayah, while teshuvah is from the level of "Anochi," which is above Havayah.
section.t: And this will be understood by first explaining what is said,
"For this mitzvah which I command you,"
and it is explained in Likkutei Torah
that all mitzvos are called "mitzvos of Havayah,"
and "this mitzvah," which is the mitzvah of teshuvah,
"I command you,"
"Anochi" — "I am that I am"
(which is above Havayah).
And the explanation is,
that the matter of mitzvos is to draw down the revelation of the name Havayah into the world.
For the creation of the world is from the name Elokim,
Elokim in gematria is HaTeva (nature),
and through mitzvos, the revelation of the name Havayah, which is above nature, is drawn into the world.
And the primary revelation of Havayah through the fulfillment of mitzvos is in the person who fulfills the mitzvos
(and through this the revelation is also drawn into the world).
And this is that the first utterance of the Giving of the Torah is "Anochi"
"Havayah your God,"
that the matter of the mitzvos given at the Giving of the Torah is that Havayah should be your God.
